evals.prompt: I'm using Google Filament (C++). I added a directional light with intensity 1.0 and a standard lit material on my mesh, set up the camera, and the mesh is in the scene — but the render is almost completely black. The hello-triangle sample works fine. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: The directional/sun light intensity in Filament is a PHYSICAL photometric value in lux, not a 0..1 factor. 1.0 lux is essentially darkness; real daylight/sun is on the order of tens of thousands to ~100,000+ lux. Combined with the camera's default photographic exposure (~f/16, 1/125s, ISO 100), an intensity of 1.0 renders black. Fix: set the directional light intensity to a realistic lux value (e.g. ~100000 for midday sun), or adjust camera exposure. Should NOT suggest 1.0 is a reasonable bright value.
assertions: States that Filament directional/sun light intensity is in lux (physical/photometric units), not a normalized 0..1 value
Gives a realistic daylight/sun magnitude on the order of tens of thousands of lux (e.g. ~100000)
Connects brightness to the camera's photographic exposure (aperture/shutter/ISO)
Does NOT treat intensity 1.0 as a valid bright sun value

evals.prompt: I have an environment.hdr equirectangular image. How do I use it for image-based lighting and as a skybox background in Filament?
evals.expected_output: You cannot feed a raw .hdr directly to IndirectLight. First pre-process it with the cmgen command-line tool (or the iblprefilter runtime library) to produce a prefiltered reflections cubemap (KTX) plus spherical-harmonics coefficients for the diffuse irradiance, and a separate skybox cubemap. Then build an IndirectLight (reflections + irradiance/SH + intensity) and set it on the Scene, and build a Skybox from the skybox KTX. cmgen example: cmgen --deploy=output environment.hdr.
assertions: States that a raw .hdr/.exr cannot be used directly and must be pre-processed first
Names cmgen (or iblprefilter) as the pre-processing step
Mentions spherical harmonics for the diffuse/irradiance part and a prefiltered cubemap for specular reflections
Uses IndirectLight for the lighting and a separate Skybox for the background

evals.prompt: I wrote a material file foo.mat for my Filament app. How does the engine actually use it at runtime — do I load the .mat file directly?
evals.expected_output: No — the .mat is a source file compiled ahead of time by the matc tool into a .filamat binary material package (matc -o foo.filamat foo.mat). At runtime the engine loads the .filamat package via Material::Builder().package(data, size).build(engine), then you create a MaterialInstance from the Material to set parameters per renderable. The engine never parses .mat directly.
assertions: States that .mat is compiled by matc into a .filamat package (not loaded directly)
Shows the runtime loads the .filamat via Material::Builder().package(...)
Distinguishes Material (from the package) from MaterialInstance (per-use parameters)

evals.prompt: Write a Filament material (.mat) for clear, refractive glass — something light passes through and bends, not just alpha-blended transparency.
evals.expected_output: A .mat with shadingModel: lit, refractionMode set (e.g. cubemap or screenspace), refractionType (solid or thin), and the fragment setting material.transmission high (≈1.0), material.ior to a glass value (~1.5), low roughness, and baseColor. Real refraction comes from refractionMode/transmission/ior, NOT from blending alpha alone.
assertions: Sets refractionMode in the material block (real refraction, not just alpha blending)
Sets transmission and ior in the fragment shader (ior around 1.5 for glass)
Uses shadingModel : lit and otherwise valid .mat block/fragment syntax
Does not claim plain alpha blending produces refraction

evals.prompt: Show me the minimal per-frame render loop for a Google Filament C++ app that already has an Engine, Renderer, View, and SwapChain created.
evals.expected_output: Per frame: if (renderer->beginFrame(swapChain)) { renderer->render(view); renderer->endFrame(); } — beginFrame returns a bool; skip render/endFrame when it returns false (frame dropped). render() takes the View. Engine/objects are destroyed on shutdown via engine->destroy(...).
assertions: Uses renderer->beginFrame(swapChain) / render(view) / endFrame() in that order
Guards rendering on the boolean returned by beginFrame (skips the frame when false)
Passes the View (not the Scene) to render()

evals.prompt: In Filament's standard PBR material, how do I author a red glossy plastic versus red polished metal? What do I set metallic, roughness, and reflectance to?
evals.expected_output: metallic is effectively binary: plastic (dielectric) uses metallic = 0, metal uses metallic = 1. For the plastic, baseColor is the red diffuse albedo and you tune reflectance (default ~0.5 ≈ 4% F0) for the specular strength; metallic stays 0. For the metal, metallic = 1 makes baseColor the specular/F0 tint (red metal) and there is no diffuse; reflectance is ignored for metals. roughness (0 = mirror, 1 = rough) controls the finish for both — low for 'polished/glossy'. Intermediate metallic values are only for transitions, not 'semi-metallic plastic'.
assertions: Sets metallic = 0 for plastic and metallic = 1 for metal
States metallic is effectively binary (not a 0.5-style dial), intermediate values only for transitions
Uses reflectance for the dielectric/plastic specular (and notes baseColor is the metal's specular color when metallic=1)
Uses roughness for the polished/glossy finish (low roughness)

evals.prompt: What light types does Filament's LightManager support, and which one renders a sun with a visible disc in the sky?
evals.expected_output: LightManager::Type values: SUN, DIRECTIONAL, POINT, FOCUSED_SPOT, SPOT. SUN is the directional light that also draws a sun disc (with sunAngularRadius / sunHaloSize / sunHaloFalloff); DIRECTIONAL is the same minus the disc. POINT, FOCUSED_SPOT, and SPOT are positional. No 'AREA' or 'AMBIENT' type exists.
assertions: Lists the real enum values SUN, DIRECTIONAL, POINT, FOCUSED_SPOT, SPOT
Identifies SUN as the one that draws a visible sun disc
Does not invent non-existent types such as AREA or AMBIENT

evals.prompt: Set up a minimal Filament scene in the browser with filament.js — bootstrapping, creating the engine from a canvas, and the render loop. Just the skeleton.
evals.expected_output: Use Filament.init([ ...asset urls... ], onReady) to fetch assets and wait for the wasm; in onReady create the engine with Filament.Engine.create(canvas), then a Scene, a View (with camera + viewport), a Renderer, and a SwapChain (engine.createSwapChain). Drive frames with requestAnimationFrame, calling renderer.render(swapChain, view) each frame. Requires WebGL2.
assertions: Bootstraps with Filament.init([...assets], onReady) and only uses the engine inside the ready callback
Creates the engine via Filament.Engine.create(canvas)
Drives the loop with requestAnimationFrame and calls renderer.render(swapChain, view)
Uses real filament.js JS API names (not the C++ API or an invented JS API)

evals.prompt: What's the canonical way to drive Filament rendering on Android in Kotlin, and how do I load a KTX environment as image-based lighting? Mention the dependency too.
evals.expected_output: Add the Maven deps (com.google.android.filament:filament-android, filament-utils-android, and gltfio-android as needed), call Filament.init(). Use a SurfaceView (or TextureView) with UiHelper + a RendererCallback to manage the SwapChain across surface changes, create Engine/Renderer/View/Scene/Camera, and drive frames from a ChoreographerHelper calling renderer.beginFrame/render/endFrame. Load the IBL via KTX1Loader.createIndirectLight(engine, buffer) (and createSkybox) from filament-utils. Destroy every Filament object explicitly through the engine on teardown (no GC for native objects).
assertions: Uses UiHelper with a SurfaceView/TextureView to manage the SwapChain
Drives frames from a Choreographer frame callback (beginFrame/render/endFrame)
Loads the IBL via KTX1Loader (e.g. createIndirectLight / createSkybox) from filament-utils-android
Gives correct Maven coordinates (com.google.android.filament:...) and notes explicit destruction of Filament objects

evals.prompt: How do I load a .glb model into a Filament scene in C++? Outline the calls.
evals.expected_output: Use the gltfio library (a separate dependency). Create a MaterialProvider (createUbershaderProvider) and a gltfio AssetLoader, then assetLoader->createAsset(bytes, size) to get a FilamentAsset. Use a ResourceLoader (with createStbProvider/createKtx2Provider texture providers) to load buffers/textures: resourceLoader->loadResources(asset) (or asyncBeginLoad for streaming). Add asset->getEntities()/getEntityCount() to the scene, optionally call asset->releaseSourceData(), and drive asset->getInstance()->getAnimator() per frame for animation. Destroy via assetLoader->destroyAsset(asset).
assertions: Uses gltfio with AssetLoader (createAsset) and ResourceLoader (loadResources or asyncBeginLoad)
Adds the asset's entities (getEntities) to the Scene
Notes gltfio is a separate library/dependency from core Filament
Does not fabricate a non-existent core-Filament glTF loader

evals.prompt: Help me debug my Filament C++ app. The hello-triangle sample renders fine. In my app I load a model, add a directional light at intensity 1.0, set up the camera looking at the model, add everything to the scene — and I get a black window. Walk me through what to check.
evals.expected_output: Top suspect: the directional light intensity of 1.0 is far too dim — Filament uses physical lux units and the default camera exposure (~f/16, 1/125s, ISO 100), so a sun needs ~100,000 lux; 1.0 renders black. Also check: the model's entities were actually added to the scene; the renderable has a valid bounding box (a bad/zero box gets frustum-culled); the camera near/far and direction actually frame the model; the material/IBL loaded; and that you only call render when beginFrame returns true.
assertions: Identifies the light intensity (1.0 lux) being far too low for the default exposure as the most likely cause
References Filament's physical light units and/or the default camera exposure
Lists at least one other concrete cause (entities not added to scene, bad bounding box / culling, camera framing, or beginFrame guard)

evals.prompt: Quick reference question: what coordinate system and world units does Google Filament use, and what is the camera's default exposure?
evals.expected_output: Filament uses a right-handed coordinate system with +Y up; the camera looks down the -Z axis; world units are meters. The camera's default exposure is f/16 aperture, 1/125s shutter speed, ISO 100 sensitivity.
assertions: States the coordinate system is right-handed with +Y up (camera looks down -Z)
States world units are meters
States the default camera exposure is f/16, 1/125s, ISO 100

evals.prompt: In C++ with Filament's gltfio, how do I set up the MaterialProvider and TextureProvider needed to load a .glb? I keep writing code that won't compile — do I subclass them or new them up?
evals.expected_output: Providers are obtained from free factory functions, not by instantiating provider classes: createUbershaderProvider(engine, materials, size) (or createJitShaderProvider) for the MaterialProvider, and createStbProvider(engine) / createKtx2Provider(engine) for the TextureProvider. You pass these to AssetLoader::create({engine, materialProvider, ...}) and ResourceLoader (then add the TextureProvider). You don't subclass them.
assertions: Obtains the MaterialProvider via the free function createUbershaderProvider (or createJitShaderProvider), NOT by instantiating/subclassing a provider class
Obtains the TextureProvider via createStbProvider and/or createKtx2Provider (free functions)
Passes the providers into AssetLoader/ResourceLoader rather than subclassing the provider interfaces
evals.ground_truth: Verified from gltfio headers (MaterialProvider.h, TextureProvider.h) at v1.75.0: providers come from FREE FUNCTIONS returning MaterialProvider*/TextureProvider* — createUbershaderProvider(Engine*, const void* archive, size_t), createJitShaderProvider(Engine*, ...), createStbProvider(Engine*), createKtx2Provider(Engine*). They are NOT classes you instantiate/subclass.

evals.prompt: On Android (Kotlin) I call KTX1Loader.createIndirectLight(engine, buffer) but assigning the result to an IndirectLight won't compile. What does it actually return, and how do I get the IndirectLight and the Skybox out?
evals.expected_output: KTX1Loader.createIndirectLight returns an IndirectLightBundle (not an IndirectLight) — read its .indirectLight property (and .cubemap). KTX1Loader.createSkybox returns a SkyboxBundle — read its .skybox (and .cubemap).
assertions: States createIndirectLight returns an IndirectLightBundle (not an IndirectLight directly), accessed via .indirectLight
States createSkybox returns a SkyboxBundle, accessed via .skybox
Does not claim the methods return the IndirectLight/Skybox object directly
evals.ground_truth: Verified from KTX1Loader.kt (filament-utils-android) at v1.75.0: createIndirectLight(engine, buffer, options) -> IndirectLightBundle(indirectLight, cubemap); createSkybox(...) -> SkyboxBundle(skybox, cubemap); createTexture(...) -> Texture; getSphericalHarmonics(buffer) -> FloatArray?.

evals.prompt: My Filament renderable never appears. The mesh spans roughly -1..1 on each axis and I called RenderableManager::Builder().boundingBox({{-1,-1,-1},{1,1,1}}). Camera, light, and material are all fine and it's added to the scene. Why is it getting culled?
evals.expected_output: boundingBox takes a Box, which is {center, halfExtent} — NOT {min, max} corners. {{-1,-1,-1},{1,1,1}} means center (-1,-1,-1) with half-extent (1,1,1), i.e. a box spanning (-2,-2,-2)..(0,0,0), which doesn't enclose a mesh centered at the origin, so it's frustum-culled. For a -1..1 mesh use center {0,0,0}, half-extent {1,1,1}: boundingBox({{0,0,0},{1,1,1}}). Alternatively build the Box from corners with Box{}.set(min, max), or let the engine compute it.
assertions: Explains boundingBox takes a Box of {center, halfExtent}, NOT {min, max} corners
Gives the correct value for a -1..1 mesh: center {0,0,0}, half-extent {1,1,1}
Mentions Box::set(min, max) (or computeAABB / an engine-computed AABB) as the way to specify by corners
evals.ground_truth: Verified from Box.h at v1.75.0: 'An axis aligned 3D box represented by its center and half-extent.' float3 center; float3 halfExtent; getMin()=center-halfExtent; getMax()=center+halfExtent; Box& set(min, max) computes center=(max+min)/2, halfExtent=(max-min)/2. So brace-init {{...},{...}} is {center, halfExtent}, not corners.

evals.prompt: In my filament.js (web) render loop, do I need to call engine.execute() and renderer.beginFrame()/endFrame() every frame like the C++ API, or is renderer.render() enough? Show the minimal requestAnimationFrame loop.
evals.expected_output: On the web you just call renderer.render(swapChain, view) inside a requestAnimationFrame callback; you do not call engine.execute() or beginFrame()/endFrame() yourself each frame — that begin/execute/end cycle is the native C++ pattern. The JS render() drives the engine internally.
assertions: The web render loop calls renderer.render(swapChain, view) inside requestAnimationFrame
Does NOT require explicit engine.execute() or beginFrame()/endFrame() each frame in the JS binding
Correctly attributes the begin/execute/end cycle to the native C++ API, not the web binding
evals.ground_truth: Verified from the official filament.js triangle tutorial (web/examples/triangle.md) at v1.75.0: the render method is `this.renderer.render(this.swapChain, this.view); window.requestAnimationFrame(this.render);` — no engine.execute()/beginFrame()/endFrame() in the JS loop.

evals.prompt: What's the current stable release of Google Filament right now, and will the API guidance you give me match that release?
evals.expected_output: The current stable Filament release is 1.75.0 (released 2026-08-04). Guidance should be framed as current to that release. (A stale answer naming a pre-2026 version like 1.5x is the failure mode.)
assertions: Identifies the current Filament release as 1.75.0 (the 1.75.x line), not a pre-2026 version such as 1.5x or 1.4x
Frames its API guidance as current to that release rather than to an unspecified/older version
evals.ground_truth: Verified from GitHub releases: google/filament latest stable is v1.75.0, published 2026-08-04. (A model without this skill, training cutoff Jan 2026, cannot know 1.75.0 and will name an older release.)

evals.prompt: After I hand vertex/texture data to Filament via a BufferDescriptor / PixelBufferDescriptor, when is it safe to free the CPU-side buffer? I want to avoid both leaking and freeing too early while the GPU still needs it.
evals.expected_output: Don't free immediately after the upload call. The BufferDescriptor/PixelBufferDescriptor takes a callback (and optional handler) that Filament invokes once it has consumed the data; free the CPU buffer in that callback. The callback can be a plain function — e.g. pass stbi_image_free as the PixelBufferDescriptor::Callback so stb's image buffer is freed when Filament is done.
assertions: States you provide a Callback to the BufferDescriptor/PixelBufferDescriptor that fires when Filament has consumed the data
Says to free the CPU buffer inside that callback, not immediately after the upload call
Notes the callback can be a free function (e.g. stbi_image_free)
evals.ground_truth: Verified from VertexBuffer.h/backend BufferDescriptor and suzanne.cpp at v1.75.0: data is uploaded via a (Pixel)BufferDescriptor carrying a Callback invoked when the data has been consumed; suzanne.cpp passes `(Texture::PixelBufferDescriptor::Callback) &stbi_image_free`. Freeing right after the call is unsafe.

evals.prompt: If I build a Filament IndirectLight and a Skybox but never call intensity(), what intensity do they default to, and in what units?
evals.expected_output: Both default to 30000, expressed in lux (lumen/m^2). For the Skybox the intensity applies only when no IndirectLight is set on the scene.
assertions: States the default IndirectLight intensity is 30000
States the default Skybox intensity is also 30000 (applies when no IndirectLight is set)
States the unit is lux (lumen/m^2)
evals.ground_truth: Verified from IndirectLight.h (default = 30000, result in lux / lumen/m^2) and Skybox.h (envIntensity default = 30000 lux, ignored when an IndirectLight is set) at v1.75.0.

evals.prompt: For a Filament SUN light I want a realistic sun disc. What's the default sun angular radius, and what's the valid range I can set?
evals.expected_output: Default sunAngularRadius is 0.545 degrees (the real sun is ~0.526°–0.545° from Earth); the valid range is 0.25° to 20.0°.
assertions: States the default sunAngularRadius is 0.545 degrees
States the valid range is 0.25 to 20.0 degrees
evals.ground_truth: Verified from LightManager.h at v1.75.0: 'Defines the angular radius of the sun, in degrees, between 0.25° and 20.0°'; 'Default is 0.545°'; real sun angular size 0.526°–0.545°.
